summary: Serialized product distribution into African markets, coordinated around controlled movement and clear hand-offs.
detail_html:
This showcase case study expands on the existing DStv project reference. The movement involved serialized products being distributed into African markets, where documentation, shipment visibility and controlled hand-offs are particularly important.

The project demonstrates how distribution can be coordinated as a connected flow rather than a series of unrelated transport bookings.

Public performance figures are not currently available, so this case study intentionally avoids invented delivery metrics.

summary: International logistics support for an annual advertising campaign spanning 30 countries.
detail_html:
A multi-country campaign creates a different logistics challenge: shared launch dates, multiple destinations and materials that need to arrive in the correct sequence.

This project demonstrates the planning required to coordinate international movements around a common campaign timeline while keeping communication consistent across markets.

The 30-country scope is based on the existing Supreme Supply project reference; the supporting narrative is showcase copy and should be validated before launch.

summary: Export and re-import coordination for a specialised international logistics requirement.
detail_html:
This project involved an international export followed by a re-import, requiring both legs to be planned as one connected process.

The case study highlights documentation continuity, milestone planning and visibility when the same goods leave a market and later return.

Detailed commercial or cargo information is not publicly available and has not been invented for this mock case study.

summary: Logistics for relocating a decommissioned chip manufacturing plant from Halifax, Canada to Johannesburg.
detail_html:
The relocation of industrial equipment from Halifax to Johannesburg illustrates the planning involved in a complex international movement.

Equipment handling, international routing, staged movement and progress communication all need to align around the wider relocation programme.

This case study is based on the project listed on Supreme Supply’s existing website; descriptive wording is showcase content.

summary: Ongoing import and export support integrated into a local manufacturer’s wider operating rhythm.
detail_html:
This relationship demonstrates the difference between managing isolated shipments and supporting an ongoing supply chain.

Recurring imports and exports can be planned around purchasing cycles, production needs and outbound commitments, giving the manufacturer more predictable logistics visibility.

The manufacturer remains unnamed because the existing website does not identify the client.

summary: Mock case study for weekly inbound replenishment and distribution into a regional retail network.
detail_html:
This fictional showcase project demonstrates how recurring inbound freight, warehousing and local distribution could be coordinated for a retail customer.

The operating model uses weekly shipment planning, receiving windows, stock release schedules and delivery milestones to reduce last-minute coordination.

Mock project: replace with a verified client example before launch.

summary: Mock case study for moving specialised mining equipment from South Africa into a neighbouring market.
detail_html:
This fictional project demonstrates the planning required for industrial equipment that crosses a regional border.

Route planning, equipment dimensions, border documentation and site-delivery requirements are considered together so the movement can be sequenced around operational constraints.

Mock project: for design demonstration only.

summary: Mock case study for importing automotive parts and distributing stock to multiple South African locations.
detail_html:
This fictional case study combines inbound sea freight, receiving, warehousing and scheduled distribution to multiple branches.

The showcase illustrates how inventory movement can be planned from port arrival through to branch-level delivery while keeping one set of shipment milestones visible to the customer.

Mock project: replace before public launch.

summary: Mock case study for an urgent component movement supporting a manufacturing production schedule.
detail_html:
This fictional example shows how an urgent air-freight movement could be coordinated when a production deadline cannot move.

The focus is on rapid routing options, document preparation, uplift visibility and immediate final-delivery coordination after clearance.

Mock project: no performance claims in this example should be treated as client history.

summary: Mock case study for consolidating stock from multiple inbound suppliers before regional distribution.
detail_html:
This fictional programme demonstrates how warehousing can be used as an active consolidation point rather than passive storage.

Inbound supplier deliveries are received into one facility, prepared around outbound schedules and released into regional distribution in planned waves.

Mock project: design demonstration only.
